clue.text: Greater than zero? Not in doubt

blocks.note: first meaning: the mathematical sense, a number above nought
second meaning: certain, sure of something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a quantity exceeds nought and is told there is no question about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the second half look like an answer to the first, but they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes numbers above nought in maths and also a person who is completely certain or convinced.

clue.text: Spies student donning underwear

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one piece is worn around another

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
pants is the British word for underpants

explanation.surface: Secret agents disguise a student by dressing them in underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun. In Britain pants are underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an undercover agent placed inside an organisation, so moles or infiltrators are plants.

clue.text: Muslim leader's rock broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so we want a word that is spoken like another

blocks.note: to rock is to shake, and this title is pronounced the same way

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader's favourite rock music is played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music or stone, but here it is the verb meaning to sway or shake. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikh is an Arab chief or a senior Islamic religious leader or scholar.

clue.text: I'm going to keep one ornamental coronet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: ta-ra is an informal British goodbye, said when leaving
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are keeping a decorative crown for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm going' reads as an intention, but it stands for a farewell: ta-ra is a northern English way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled semicircular headband worn by women, a small crown for formal occasions.

clue.text: Wicked enemy of Birmingham team at home

blocks.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, known simply as Villa
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A football fan calls a rival side's supporter the wicked enemy of the Birmingham club playing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English Premier League football team from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is the evil character in a story, the bad guy who opposes the hero.

clue.text: Bad storm around North Carolina

indicators.note: one thing placed around another surrounds it

blocks.note: to storm a place is to raid it
NC is the US postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A dangerous weather system is gathering over North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather, but it is the verb for attacking a building suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid describes butter or fat that has gone off and smells unpleasant, so food that is spoilt.

clue.text: Stars with wild dream accepting Oscar

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so a letter is put inside
something wild is out of control, so these letters run in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: with and 'and' both mean together alongside
taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Film stars have wild dreams of winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'Oscar' conjure Hollywood, but the stars are in the night sky and Oscar is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation in the northern sky, a named group of stars, and also the neighbouring galaxy.

clue.text: One dining on his own?

blocks.note: surface reading: a solitary diner eating alone at a table
setter's reading: eating his own kind, feeding on fellow humans

explanation.walkthrough: 'On his own' suggests eating alone; read it as 'eating his own (people)' and the diner becomes a man-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh feeds on members of their own species, hence 'his own'.

clue.text: Old PM departs from Haifa?

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
Haifa is a city in Israel, so someone from there is Israeli

explanation.surface: A former prime minister leaves the port of Haifa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departs from' reads as a single phrase about leaving, but it splits: 'departs' is D and 'from Haifa' describes a nationality. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister, leading the Conservatives twice in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Last word by competent subject

blocks.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word
competent and able both mean capable

explanation.surface: A capable person gets the final say on a topic under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a noun for a topic, but it is the adjective, as in 'subject to the law'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable can mean answerable or liable to something, as in amenable to the law, which matches being subject to it.

clue.text: Beautiful boy Batty said no

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so these letters are jumbled out of their right order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A handsome young man named Batty turned someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' is capitalised to pass as a surname, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a strikingly handsome youth loved by Aphrodite, and the name now means any very good-looking young man.

clue.text: Satirical piece in second gear

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
kit is equipment or clothing, so gear

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch is performed with a car in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second gear' suggests driving; split it into an abbreviation and a word for equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that parodies or mocks something, often performed on stage or television.

clue.text: Surprise – ready to keep ace and not lead

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to surprise someone is to take them aback
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go' or 'all set'
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A card player springs a surprise by holding on to an ace and declining to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' sounds like a card-play term, but 'not lead' is the definition of the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a back seat is an idiom for letting others be in charge and staying in a less prominent role.

clue.text: Consent from Macron and Merz for board

blocks.note: Macron is the French president, and oui is French for yes
Merz is the German chancellor, and ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: The French and German leaders both agree to a proposal from the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmanuel Macron leads France and Friedrich Merz leads Germany, so their 'yes' comes in their own languages. 'Consent from' applies to both names.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to receive supposed messages from spirits; the name joins French and German words for yes.

clue.text: Prepare lamb initially placed in wok

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
something placed in a vessel sits inside it

blocks.note: a wok is a type of cooking pan
the first letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: get the lamb ready by first putting it in the wok.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe step, but 'Prepare' is the definition, not part of the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to work out arrangements for it in advance, so to get ready or prepare.

clue.text: Cleansed Dane ruled in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A freshly washed Dane held sway at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination, but read it as re-sort: sort the letters again.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash and iron them, so laundered items have been cleaned.

clue.text: Cover for little piggy?

blocks.note: surface reading: a coat or shelter for a small pig
setter's reading: the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy' counts toes, so the piggy is a toe and the cover is the hard plate on top of it

explanation.walkthrough: In the children's rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', each piggy is one of a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard keratin plate on the upper tip of each toe covers and protects it.

clue.text: Spooner's discovered everything in ruin

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: discovered is found and everything is all; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Someone uncovered every detail about a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening consonants of 'down fall' and you get 'fown dall', which is close to how 'found all' is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a loss of power, status or fortune, so a person's undoing or collapse.

clue.text: Part of an Arsenal crowd turning up in a resting place

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upwards means reading from the bottom to the top
a piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
taken as written
a tomb is a final resting place for the dead

explanation.surface: Some Arsenal football fans show up at a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, so 'Arsenal crowd' suggests fans; the capital is a disguise for a stockpile of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon forms part of a nation's arsenal, its collection of weapons and munitions.

clue.text: Push out doubter after Reformation

indicators.note: something that has undergone reformation has been formed anew into a different shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious sceptic is expelled following the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R points to the sixteenth-century church movement, but it simply means the letters are re-formed.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust something forward or stick it out, a formal verb for pushing outwards.

clue.text: Fish slumber mostly facing north

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, facing north points upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: slumber and sleep are synonyms

explanation.surface: Fish mostly sleep with their heads pointing north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is a plural noun here; drop the last letter of the synonym and read it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish found in rivers and the sea.

clue.text: See 12
Sailor in small tub – time to rest

indicators.note: a piece put in another sits inside it

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a tub is a bathtub

explanation.surface: A sailor relaxes in a tiny bathtub, taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor sits between the two other pieces, so the abbreviation for small comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of religious observance on which work is forbidden, a day set aside for rest.

clue.text: Student body keeps a little storage in cloud

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
MB, a megabyte, is a small amount of computer storage

explanation.surface: A students' union keeps a small amount of data stored in the cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloud' suggests online storage, which fits the surface, but it is the definition: a rain cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbus is a meteorological term for a large grey rain-bearing cloud, and also a halo of light.

clue.text: Money once raised in late September

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, lying across their boundary
in a down clue, something raised is lifted upwards, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Funds that used to be collected towards the end of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' tells us the currency is no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain until it was replaced by the euro in 2002.

clue.text: Wanderer compos mentis in "Glesga"?

indicators.note: Glaswegian speech says 'no' for 'not', dropping the final consonant of that word

blocks.note: compos mentis is Latin for of sound mind, that is sane, not mad

explanation.surface: A traveller who is perfectly sane, described in the Glasgow accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Glesga is the local pronunciation of Glasgow, where Scots say 'no' for 'not'; so someone sane is 'no mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person with no fixed home who moves from place to place, so a wanderer.

clue.text: Seducer left island: knight embraced by Edward VII

indicators.note: something embraced is held within another's arms, so it sits inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I is the abbreviation for island
Bertie was the family nickname of King Edward VII
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A womaniser fled an island after a knight was hugged by King Edward VII.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward VII, Queen Victoria's son, was known as Bertie from his first name Albert, and was himself a famous womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a man who lives a dissolute life of sexual pleasure without moral restraint, so a seducer.

clue.text: Cyclist free here in the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only its central letters are used

blocks.note: to free someone of something is to rid them of it
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides without restriction through the centre of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective but works as the verb meaning to clear or release.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a bicycle rides it, so a cyclist is a bike rider.

clue.text: British rower in a delta on boat

indicators.note: pieces placed in another sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British
an oar, or oarsman, is a crossword word for a rower
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A British oarsman paddles in a river delta in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A rower can mean the oar itself, which pulls through the water; 'delta' is a letter, not a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a ship, train or aircraft, so being on a boat.

clue.text: Jawbone broken in bedlam

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's jaw was fractured during a chaotic brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the anatomical name for the lower jaw bone in humans and other vertebrates.

clue.text: Drive in the same place taking look around

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece encloses another
a piece placed around another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'
ibid, from Latin ibidem, means in the same place in citations

explanation.surface: Someone drives round the same spot, taking a look around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' reads as a verb about motoring, but it is a noun meaning an urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, the psychological urge or appetite that psychologists call a drive.

clue.text: Attractive quality is in entrance area

indicators.note: a piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to entrance someone is to charm or enchant them
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An appealing feature can be found in the lobby of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance area' looks like a doorway or foyer, but 'entrance' is the verb meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm that draws and inspires others, a magnetic appeal.
